To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the maximum residual stress in SLM of 316L is located at the powder bed-baseplate interface and it can be decreased by decreasing the hatch spacing and increasing the scanning speed.
the thermal and residual stress profiles in selective laser melting are highly dependent on the laser power, scanning speed, hatch spacing and powder bed height.
the thermal and residual stresses are highly sensitive to the process parameters.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a realistic multi track and multi layer SLM FEM model and its application for investigating the influence of various process parameters on thermal, cooling and residual stress profile.
the parametric investigation of thermal as well as the residual stress profile during the SLM process of 316L steel.
the parametric study of thermal and stress profile in a selective laser melting process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the maximum residual stresses can be reduced by increasing the laser power and decreasing the scanning speed and hatch spacing.

increasing the laser power or decreasing the scanning speed both results in an increased thermal gradient and cooling rate, which results in an increase in maximum temperature as well as residual stresses.
the maximum melt pool temperature increases with an increase in laser energy input.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the thermal profile and residual stress profile are influenced by the process parameters in a nonlinear fashion.
a higher laser power, a lower scanning speed or a lower hatch spacing results in a higher melt pool temperature.
the maximum melt pool temperature is a direct function of the laser power and scanning speed.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a proper selection of the processing parameters is required to achieve the desired stress levels and to avoid crack formation during SLM processing of 316L.
the thermal profile can be controlled by varying laser power or scanning velocity, while residual stress profile can be controlled through hatch spacing.
the FEM model can be used for a parametric study of thermal and residual profile in selective laser melted 316L stainless steels.
